cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, just heard from the LORD how his brother Aaron goes into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement for Israel's sins (Leviticus 16:2, 17, 34). Now the LORD has a new message for Aaron, Aaron's sons and all the Israelites. That's the WHOLE group chat, friend, so nobody gets to say they missed the message.

cards.question: Say someone from the house of Israel slaughters an ox, a lamb or a goat, in the camp or outside it. God says he must bring it somewhere instead, to present it as an offering to the LORD. Where?

answers.text: The entrance to the Tent of Meeting
The banks of the Jordan River

cards.question: God says a man who slaughters an ox, a lamb or a goat without bringing it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting has shed blood and must be cut off from his people.
God says the Israelites will now bring the LORD the sacrifices they've been offering somewhere else. Where have they been offering them?

cards.text: Now those sacrifices come to the priest at the entrance, as peace offerings. The priest splatters the blood on the LORD's altar and burns the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Then God names what has to stop: "They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat demons to which they have prostituted themselves."

cards.question: God says this rule about where to bring sacrifices only lasts as long as Moses leads Israel.
God says anyone who offers a burnt offering or sacrifice but doesn't bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting must be cut off from his people, even a foreigner living among the Israelites.

cards.text: Now God turns to blood: if anyone eats any blood, Israelite or foreigner, God says, "I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people." Friend, I got slid into a junk drawer and cut off from my whole family once, and I would NOT recommend it.

cards.question: Then God explains why eating blood is off-limits. What reason does He give?

answers.text: The life of the flesh is in the blood
The sickness of the flesh is in the blood
The curse of the ground is in the blood

cards.question: God says He has given the blood to the Israelites to make atonement for their souls. Where?

cards.text: God says it AGAIN: no Israelite and no foreigner living among them may eat blood. A hunter who brings down a wild animal or bird that may be eaten has to drain its blood and cover it with dirt. Then God says it once more: the life of all flesh is its blood, so no one may eat the blood of any living thing. Friend, when somebody keeps saying the same thing, that's the part you write on your hand.

Then a different case: someone, native or foreigner, eats something found dead or mauled by wild beasts. He has to wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he's unclean until evening, then he's clean. That's laundry day AND bath night, friend, back to back. If he skips it, God says "he shall bear his iniquity."
That's the end of this message, friend. But trust me, the LORD's not done talking to Moses, so keep that apron on.
